_comment: Return ranges are broad teaching assumptions, not current quotes. Re-check these facts and government or bank rates on official websites before every demo.

ideas.name: Savings account / liquid fund
ideas.school_explanation: A safe piggy bank you can open any day. A liquid fund is an investment that can usually be sold quickly. Bank deposits and funds have different risks.
ideas.real_life_example: Keep school-trip money in a place you can reach quickly.
ideas.money_access: Usually same day for a bank account; fund timing varies
how_to_start: Keep emergency cash in a bank.
Compare fees and access rules.
Check deposit protection and fund risks.

quiz.question: What is this useful for?
Can every liquid fund promise a fixed rate?

ideas.name: Fixed Deposit (FD) or Recurring Deposit (RD)
ideas.school_explanation: A piggy bank locked by the bank for a fixed time. The bank pays interest for waiting. Taking money out early may have a cost.
ideas.real_life_example: Like saving festival money in a sealed jar until the date you chose.
ideas.money_access: At maturity; early withdrawal rules vary
how_to_start: Compare rates with your bank.
Choose an amount and end date.
Read early withdrawal rules.

quiz.question: When is an FD meant to end?
Can an early exit have a cost?

ideas.name: Public Provident Fund (PPF)
ideas.school_explanation: A government savings plan with a long lock-in. It can suit patient saving. The government sets its rate and may change it.
ideas.real_life_example: Like planting a tree and waiting many years before picking fruit.
how_to_start: Check current rules on the official site.
Open an account with an approved provider.
Add money within the yearly limits.

quiz.question: Is PPF a short-term account?
Where should you check its current rate?

ideas.name: Debt (bond) mutual funds
ideas.school_explanation: You lend money through a fund to companies or governments. They pay interest, but the fund price can still move.
ideas.real_life_example: A group of classmates lend small amounts together and share repayments.
ideas.money_access: Usually a few working days; rules vary
how_to_start: Learn how the fund lends money.
Check fees and risk details.
Use a registered platform.

quiz.question: Can a debt fund's value fall?
What does a bond mean here?

ideas.name: Index fund SIP
ideas.school_explanation: You buy tiny parts of many companies each month. An index fund follows a group of companies. Its value can rise or fall.
ideas.real_life_example: Like picking a whole cricket team instead of betting on one player.
ideas.money_access: Usually a few working days; market value changes
how_to_start: Learn what index the fund follows.
Check fees and fund details.
Choose an affordable monthly amount.

quiz.question: What does an index fund usually hold?
Does a SIP guarantee profit?

ideas.name: Equity mutual funds (flexi cap / large cap)
ideas.school_explanation: A fund manager picks many company shares for you. The value can move a lot. Longer time may help, but cannot promise profit.
ideas.real_life_example: Like a coach choosing a team from many players.
ideas.money_access: Usually a few working days; market value changes
how_to_start: Read the fund's risk label.
Compare fees and holdings.
Invest only money you can leave for years.

quiz.question: Who chooses shares in an active fund?
Are high returns guaranteed?

ideas.name: Gold (gold ETF / gold fund)
ideas.school_explanation: A gold fund follows gold prices without keeping jewellery at home. Gold prices can also fall, so it is one part of a mix.
ideas.real_life_example: Like keeping a spare umbrella, useful sometimes but not needed for every job.
ideas.money_access: Usually a few working days; price changes
how_to_start: Learn how the fund tracks gold.
Check fees and taxes.
Keep gold as one part, not the whole plan.

quiz.question: Does gold always go up?
Why might someone hold some gold?

ideas.name: ELSS (tax saving mutual fund)
ideas.school_explanation: An equity fund with a three-year lock-in for each investment. It may help with tax under current rules, but rules can change.
ideas.real_life_example: Like a school library book you must keep for a set time before returning.
ideas.money_access: Each payment is locked for 3 years
how_to_start: Check current tax rules with an official source.
Compare fund risks and fees.
Invest only after keeping emergency savings.

quiz.question: How long is each ELSS payment locked?
Does tax eligibility stay the same forever?

ideas.name: NPS (National Pension System)
ideas.school_explanation: A long-term plan for money after work. It has rules about when money can come out. Learn the rules before joining.
ideas.real_life_example: Like putting aside a little now for your future self.
cons: Rules and tax treatment can change
how_to_start: Read the current official NPS rules.
Choose a registered account provider.
Pick a mix that fits your time and comfort.

quiz.question: What is NPS mainly for?
Can money access have restrictions?

ideas.name: Direct stocks (advanced)
ideas.school_explanation: You own a small piece of one company. Its price can rise or fall a lot. Learn first and never depend on one company.
ideas.real_life_example: Like choosing one player for a team instead of the whole team.
ideas.money_access: Market hours; price changes and sale rules apply
how_to_start: Learn how a company earns money.
Practice without real money first.
Do not buy because of a tip.

quiz.question: Does this app name a stock to buy?
Can one company share fall sharply?

special_jars.name: Emergency fund top-up
special_jars.reason: Keep money for surprise costs where you can reach it.

special_jars.name: Pay off high-interest debt
special_jars.reason: Paying costly debt can reduce future interest.
